summary_alerts.consensus_buy_GOOGL: Four members spanning both parties—Capito (R), Fetterman (D), Taylor (R), and Keating (D)—independently accumulated Alphabet (GOOGL) positions during the window, an unusually broad cross-party convergence that elevates this above routine portfolio overlap. Four-member agreement is the strongest consensus buy signal observed in the current cohort.
summary_alerts.consensus_buy_HD: Home Depot (HD) attracted cross-party accumulation from Khanna (D), McCormick (R), and Taylor (R), with a combined disclosed buy volume of roughly $99K. The convergence on a housing-adjacent consumer name suggests shared expectations of durable home-improvement demand across political lines.
summary_alerts.consensus_buy_MSFT: Microsoft (MSFT) was purchased independently by Fetterman (D), Taylor (R), and McCormick (R), underscoring continued confidence in enterprise cloud and AI infrastructure among members with access to relevant policy discussions. The three-member cross-party signal places MSFT among the higher-conviction buys in the 60-day window.
summary_alerts.consensus_sell_AAPL: Apple (AAPL) saw cross-party selling from Suozzi (D) and Taylor (R), both disclosing disposals during the same window, with a combined disclosed value of approximately $40K. Concurrent reductions across party lines in the most widely held U.S. equity may reflect profit-taking after an extended valuation premium, caution around antitrust or tariff exposure, or routine rebalancing.
summary_alerts.consensus_sell_T: AT&T (T) was sold by Fetterman (D) and Taylor (R) within the window for a combined disclosed value near $16K, producing a cross-party sell signal in legacy telecommunications. The paired disposal may reflect reduced conviction amid fiber-buildout capital demands and intensifying broadband competition.
summary_alerts.consensus_sell_WAT: Waters Corporation (WAT) was disposed of by Dingell (D) and Hern (R) during the window, a cross-party sell in the analytical-instruments segment that may reflect shared concerns about margin compression or capital-equipment demand in life sciences tooling.
summary_alerts.conviction_Hern_TXN: Kevin Hern's concentration in Texas Instruments (TXN) at roughly $750K is the single largest individual-name disclosure in the cohort and sits well outside the cohort's typical position size. A single-member commitment of this scale is noteworthy given Hern's Ways and Means seat and tax-policy exposure to the semiconductor capex cycle.
